title: Perf and correctness regression detection across driver variants
content:
Purpose
This note captures an ad-hoc investigation and proposed detection strategy for subtle performance and correctness regressions that appear only under specific GPU driver + CUDA combinations across cloud SKUs (A100 / H100 / L40S). Goal is to define reproducible checks, lightweight smoke tests, and operational gating for driver rollouts.

Motivation / Background
- We observed two customer incidents in Q3 where tail latency and occasional truncated token sequences correlated with recent driver rollouts in a single region. No obvious host-level resource saturation.
- Existing sku-bench artifacts cover throughput and tail-latency at macro scale, but we lack a focused, deterministic correctness check that catches bit-level/behavioral drift caused by driver/CUDA subtlety (e.g., FP path reordering, cuBLAS kernel selection differences).

High-level hypothesis
- There are three classes of failures: performance regressions (kernel launch latency, increased p99), numerical-behavior divergence (slight token-probability shifts leading to downstream beam search differences), and soft-faults (rare truncated outputs / early EOS) that are more likely with certain driver+cuda combos on specific SKUs.

Test harness design (what we implemented)
1) Deterministic workload: a fixed corpus of prompts (200 short prompts + 50 long-context prompts) that exercise prefill + decode paths and KV-cache reuse. Prompts stored in harness repo.
2) Checksum-based correctness: for each prompt we compute SHA256 over the canonical token-id sequence returned by a deterministic decoding policy (greedy or fixed-seed top-k). We maintain a baseline hashset per model+quantization+CUDA combo. Any hash divergence is a signal for investigation.
3) Microbench metrics collected per-request: prefill_time_ms, first_token_ms, per_token_ms (mean/p50/p90/p99), kernel_launch_count, cuda_sync_overhead_ms, host-to-device-copy-ms, nvlink_latency-ms when applicable. Also capture model logits L2-distance to baseline for the first 16 tokens to quantify numerical drift.
4) Telemetry hooks: attach driver version, CUDA runtime version, GPU UUID, SKU name, host kernel version, and environment variables (e.g., CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG) to each run.
5) Platform sweeps: runs across AWS p4d+p5, GCP a2/h3 families, Azure ND/ND A100/L40S offerings where available. Each run executed under multiple driver builds (the latest GA and the previous 2 stable builds) and multiple CUDA runtimes where the cloud image supported both.

Key findings (summary)
- Performance: On H100 with driver 535 + CUDA 12.2 we saw ~12% increase in median decode time for beam size 1 compared to driver 525 + CUDA 11.8 on the same instant-type under otherwise-identical config. The p99 widened by ~28% in sustained 90% load. Kernel launch latency histograms showed a ~50us shift on many small kernels (attention softmax / rotary kernels) — consistent with a different kernel selection path.
- Numerical drift: For a 7B quantized model (int8-compatible path) on A100, one driver variant produced non-identical logits at token positions 5-12 with L2 distance in the 1e-3 range; SHA256 of token sequences still matched because the decoding policy had threshold insensitivity. However, beam-search with beam=4 produced different top sequence for 3 out of 200 prompts, indicating that small numerical drift can surface under non-deterministic decoders.
- Soft-faults / truncation: On L40S images with driver X (cloud-rolled image: driver 540) we observed rare (0.4% of runs) truncated responses where the server returned an early EOS token due to an apparent NVLINK transfer glitch combined with a host timeout path. These were reproducible under our harness by enabling stress I/O concurrently on host (small host-to-device DMA jitter amplified the condition).
- Environment sensitivity: The presence/absence of CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG and different cudnn heuristics toggles changed kernel candidate selection and sometimes flipped the regression on or off.

Investigation artifacts (what we collected)
- Per-run logs (timestamped) with driver/cuda/runtime metadata and kernel timings (Nsight Systems traces for a subset).
- eBPF traces correlated with host-side interrupts and PCIe link status during failing runs.
- Small repro case that deterministically reproduces the L40S truncation when the host performs repeated small-file I/O (still in repro/confirm stage).

Risk thresholds and signal rules (proposal for auto-detection)
- Correctness alert: any SHA256 token-sequence mismatch for >= 1% of canonical prompts OR any beam-search divergence rate > 0.5% triggers P0 triage.
- Numerical drift alert: average logit L2 distance over first-16 tokens > 5e-4 AND correlated p99 latency regression > 15% => in_review with infra and driver owners.
- Soft-fault alert: observed truncated/opposite-EOS events > 0.1% in nightly smoke runs => immediate rollback candidate.

Operational recommendations
1) Nightly driver-variant smoke matrix: run the deterministic harness across the latest 3 driver builds + supported CUDA runtimes for each SKU available in our regions. Store hash artifacts in an immutable bucket and diff automatically.
2) Canary gating: integrate checksum and p99 delta checks into the canary pipeline for driver/OS image rollouts in regions; fail rollouts if thresholds are exceeded.
3) Telemetry change: ensure every production inference event includes driver hash and CUDA runtime version in trace metadata so post-mortem can group by variant.
4) Developer tooling: add a 'baseline-compare' CLI that runs a small prompt set locally and produces a human-readable digest: mismatches, L2 distances, and kernel-launch histograms.
5) Vendor engagement: for reproducible truncation cases, file a coordinated vendor support ticket including Nsight traces and eBPF captures (we have preliminary traces attached to INF-2345).

Short-term action items (owners and ETA)
- Build nightly smoke matrix job (Marco Liu) -> prototype by 2024-11-15, rollout to all regions by 2024-12-01.
- Implement baseline artifact storage + diff service (Ayesha Khan) -> 2024-11-22.
- Add driver/cuda metadata tags to production traces (Tom Becker / infra) -> 2024-10-20 (already partially done).
- Repro L40S truncation and escalate to vendor (Sofia Patel) -> repro PR opened, ticket filed INF-2345, follow-up meeting w/ vendor booked.

Longer-term ideas
- Integrate representative mini-eval sets (simple downstream tasks) into the harness to catch subtle behavioral regressions that checksums may miss.
- Explore model-level synthetic stress patterns (small warmup arrays + rapid interleaved small-decoding jobs) to surface race-sensitive kernel scheduling issues.
- Add a GPU firmware/BIOS checksum field to our host inventory so we can correlate regressions with lower-level firmware changes.

Appendix: quick commands and notes
- How to run locally: ./tools/baseline-compare --model gpt-small --prompts testset/200 --cuda 12.2 --driver 535 -> produces hashes.json and l2_summary.txt
- Nsight capture flags we used: --trace=cuda,mem,os --sample=kernel-launch --duration 120s
- eBPF probes: pci_pm_status, pci_link_state, do_softirq, nvhost_dma_submission (probes are in tools/ebpf/traces)
